title: Oak leaf motif
subtitle: A flat lobed oak leaf in dk green or rust, 9 cm long
excerpt: The oak leaf works from a centre chain spine outward, building the characteristic lobed edge with dc, htr, and tr stitches of increasing height at each lobe and decreasing back down between lobes. The five-lobed outline at 9 cm is unmistakably oak, and the flat applique can be used singly or grouped in clusters on autumnal throws and garlands.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), crochet leaf motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet botanical applique chapter.
heroPrompt: A crochet oak leaf applique in rust-orange DK cotton, 9 cm long with five clear lobes, photographed flat on natural linen in soft autumn daylight.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished oak leaf measures 9 cm long and 6 cm wide at the widest lobe pair in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Oak leaf motif
chartDefinition.caption: Foundation chain spine. Stitches increase in height at each lobe (dc at lobe base, htr up the side, tr at lobe tip) and decrease back down between lobes. Five lobes on each side, with a two-chain stem at the base.

glossaryTerms.definition: A foundation chain running the length of a leaf motif, around which stitches are worked on both sides to form the leaf shape.

content.text: The oak leaf is worked around a
centre spine

of 18 chains, building the lobed outline by varying stitch height. Each lobe rises from dc at the base, through htr on the lobe sides, to tr at the lobe tip, then decreases back to dc before the next inter-lobe notch. Five lobes per side give the unmistakable oak profile. A ch-2 stem at the base is an optional extension.

attrs.title: Materials for one leaf
attrs.body: About 7 g of DK cotton in green, rust, or gold. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished oak leaf measures 9 cm long and 6 cm wide at the widest lobe pair in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet".
Pattern
Foundation
Ch 18. Sl st into the 2nd and 3rd ch from hook (stem). This positions the hook at the first lobe base.
First side — from base to leaf tip

Working along the spine chain toward the tip: *Dc in 2 ch. Htr in 1 ch. Tr in 1 ch (lobe tip). Htr in 1 ch. Dc in 1 ch. Sl st in 1 ch (lobe notch). Dc in 1 ch.* Repeat to create 5 lobes along the first side, ending at the chain tip. (5 lobe tips on first side.)
Leaf tip
At the chain tip, work 3dc to turn the corner. Continue along the underside of the spine chain toward the stem, working 5 more lobes as above — mirroring the first side.
Stem
At the base end, sl st into the 2 remaining stem chains. Sl st to close. Fasten off.

definition.title: Oak leaf motif
definition.caption: 18ch spine. Five lobes per side: dc-htr-tr-htr-dc with sl-st notch between. 3dc at tip. 2ch stem at base.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in ends. Steam-block flat to open the lobes. Sew onto the base fabric through the outer edge.
Care
Handwash with the base fabric in cool water. Re-steam-block the leaf if the lobes close in after washing.
What to try next

The maple leaf (crochet-leaf-maple) has a five-pointed star silhouette using the same spine approach. The holly leaf (crochet-leaf-holly) has sharper, more regular points and pairs with a red berry French knot.
